Four bugs found in git diff main...HEAD. I read the code directly, because this is a four-file, 94-line change with no CLAUDE.md files, and I haven't run it. Each bug follows from the code as written.

1. canVoid is inverted, so non-admins can void invoices and admins can't (guards.js, canVoid)

app.js:28 A successful send is invisible and leaves the sent lines in place. After a 2xx response the handler only increments sentCount, which is never read anywhere in the payload. There is no success message, the list is not cleared, and the button has no sending state. A successful void (app.js:34) is also silent. Add lines, click Send invoice. Nothing on screen changes. The user cannot tell success from a dead button, and a second click re-posts the same lines.

app.js:31 The void request has no invoice identifier and no body, and the permission check exists only on the client. POST /api/invoices/void is sent with nothing saying which invoice to void. The only authorization is the client-side canVoid on a user object defined in the browser, so a direct request bypasses it. The success path also gives no feedback and does not clear lines.

" needs to become ", and ' should be escaped too.

I didn't flag the unused sentCount or the alert() calls. They're style issues, not correctness bugs.
render() puts the result inside a double-quoted attribute: title="${escapeHtml(l.client)}".

app.js:10 Totals are computed with floating-point arithmetic on money values, and fractional or huge quantities are not bounded. Summing qty*price in floats accumulates rounding error. For example, 3 × 0.1 gives 0.30000000000000004, and the per-line and total toFixed(2) displays can disagree by a cent across many lines. The amount that gets sent is the raw floats, not the rounded cents, so the server total can differ from the one shown. Integer cents should be used.

app.js:31 The void action is gated only by a client-side role check on a hard-coded user, and it sends no invoice id. The user object is a literal in browser JS, so the authorization check is meaningless. Anyone can call the endpoint, and the server must enforce roles itself. The POST to /api/invoices/void has no body or id, so it cannot say which invoice to void. There is also no confirmation prompt for a destructive action.
It stays 0, so Date.now() - 0 is never below 1000 and tooSoon() always returns false.

app.js:33 Void is a one-click destructive action with no confirmation, no target and no success state. index.html:24 renders Void invoice next to Send invoice with identical styling (styles.css:4). The request body names no invoice. The handler gives no feedback on success (line 34 handles only failure). For a user who fails canVoid the click silently does nothing. A mis-click next to Send invoice voids an invoice immediately. The request carries no invoice id, so the server cannot tell which invoice is meant. The user sees no confirmation either way.

lastSend = Date.now() needs to be set when a send starts, or after it succeeds.

3. validQuantity accepts values that aren't valid quantities (guards.js:17-19, used at app.js:17-18).
A client name such as x" onmouseover="alert(1) is not escaped, so it breaks out of the attribute and adds an event handler. This is script injection through the client field.

app.js:26 Send has no catch for a network failure and no success feedback; empty invoices are sent. Traced: a rejected fetch (offline) throws inside the async handler, becomes an unhandled rejection and shows no message; only !res.ok is handled. On success (app.js:28) nothing is shown and lines are not cleared. Driven: with lines empty, Send POSTed '[]'. User goes offline and clicks Send: nothing happens, no message. On success the user sees nothing and may click again, sending a duplicate. Send with no lines posts an empty invoice.

index.html:21 The whole list is re-announced on every add because render replaces all of its markup. app.js:7 sets list.innerHTML for the whole list on every submit, and aria-live="polite" on the ul makes a screen reader read the replaced content. With 10 lines present, adding the 11th makes a screen reader read all 11 items again, and the changed total is not announced with it.

app.js:19 Invalid quantity or price is dropped silently; the form just does nothing. The submit handler returns with no message, no aria-live text, no focus move and no aria-invalid. Quantity and price inputs have no required or type (index.html:16,18), so native validation does not step in either. Type price 1,50 (decimal comma, a common locale) or abc, and click Add line. Number("1,50") is NaN, the handler returns, and the user sees no line added and no reason why. Screen-reader users get no signal at all.

app.js:33 Void is a one-click irreversible action with no confirmation and no invoice identified. The click handler posts straight away with no body naming an invoice. In index.html:23-24 the Void button sits directly beside Send with the same style (styles.css:4 gives all buttons the same look). A mis-click on Void, next to Send invoice, voids with no confirm or undo. The request carries no invoice id, so which invoice is voided is up to the server's session state.
